program_summary: A 16-day hands-on program building real ML and AI applications — from data pipelines and model training to deployed Streamlit apps and REST APIs. Each day ends with a shippable artifact.

day.title: Build a Credit Card Fraud Detection App
day.objective: Load and clean a real transaction dataset, train a machine-learning classifier to detect fraudulent transactions, and wrap it in a simple interactive Streamlit app that predicts whether a new transaction is fraud or legitimate.
day.task_description:
Using the creditcard_2023.csv dataset, build a Streamlit application that:
1. Loads the dataset with pandas and performs basic data-quality checks (missing values, duplicates, invalid labels).
2. Cleans the data appropriately (drop the id column, handle duplicates/bad rows).
3. Trains a classification model (e.g. Random Forest) on the V1-V28 and Amount features to predict the Class label (0 = legit, 1 = fraud), using a train/test split.
4. Provides a form where the user can enter transaction feature values and get a prediction (Fraud or Legit) with a confidence score.
5. Reports model performance (precision, recall, or F1 on a held-out test set), keeping in mind the dataset is imbalanced.
day.expected_output: A running Streamlit app that loads the data, trains a fraud-detection model, and lets the user submit a transaction and receive a fraud/legit prediction with a confidence score, along with some view of the model's performance.
day.evaluation_criteria:
1. The data is loaded and cleaned correctly, with data-quality checks performed.
2. A classification model is trained properly on a train/test split, and class imbalance is acknowledged or handled.
3. The app produces predictions with confidence scores through a working Streamlit interface.
4. Model performance is reported using appropriate metrics (precision/recall/F1, not just accuracy, given the imbalance).
5. The code is well-structured and runs without errors.
day.research_topics:
pandas data loading and cleaning
scikit-learn classifiers (Random Forest) and train/test split
handling imbalanced datasets (class_weight, precision/recall vs accuracy)
Streamlit forms, widgets, and layout
day.unlock_condition: Streamlit app runs, makes predictions with confidence scores, and reports F1/precision/recall.
